As there is no central record of purchases by individual units, the military has to ⁠impose a blanket ban, Der Spiegel reported.

item.description:
China and ASEAN make progress on South China Sea pact but can't finish talks this year
Regional diplomats say China and Southeast Asian countries have made progress on a South China Sea pact but won’t be able to conclude negotiations this year as agreedByJIM GOMEZ Associated PressNovember 10, 2026, 10:01 PM
MANILA, Philippines -- China and Southeast Asian countries have made progress on a South China Sea pact but won't be able to conclude decades of negotiations this year as agreed, three regional diplomats said Wednesday.
China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations began negotiating the so-called “code of conduct” in 2005 to prevent occasional confrontations in the disputed waters from turning into a major conflict that could threaten Asia’s economies. The accord mainly calls for self-restraint and discourages aggressive acts that could spark clashes in the waterway that is a key global trade route.
After years of closed-door negotiations, which at times were delayed due to tense clashes in the contested waters, China and ASEAN agreed in 2023 to speed up the negotiations and conclude the talks by this year.
Three senior Southeast Asian diplomats with direct knowledge of the negotiations told The Associated Press that after the final round of this year's talks last month, China and the ASEAN have provisionally agreed on about 80% of all the paragraphs that will be included in the agreement.
The last major sticking points are the geographic scope to be covered by the agreement, the definition of sensitive terms and whether the accord should be legally binding or not, according to the three diplomats. They spoke on condition of anonymity and without elaborating because they were not authorized to discuss the issues in public.

Watch: Republicans vote to block Hegseth impeachment from reaching full voteByBernd Debusmann Jr, White House reporter and Ana Faguy, Reporting fromCapitol HillPublished11 November 2026, 00:38 GMTUpdated 6 hours ago
An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill.
A majority of the House of Representatives agreed to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky - for now.
In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage".
The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump.
Massie was the only Republican to vote against moving the resolution to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee on Tuesday.
His effort failed in a 211-204 vote, with more than a dozen members, including 11 Democrats, missing the vote.
The move to send the measure to the panel effectively kills the effort, as there is only a short period of time left in this Congress before Democrats take control in January.
President Trump celebrated the vote in a post on Truth Social, saying the effort "has miserably FAILED".
"Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot," Trump said, referring to Hegseth.
After the vote, Massie said he "wasn't surprised" but "was disappointed", according to BBC's US media partner CBS.

Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents.
Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning.
US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show.
Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device.
The BBC has contacted his representatives.
Griffin described Markle's housing situation as "untenable", writing in the order revoking his pretrial release that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court".
He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician".
"Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday.
"We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," he added.
Markle, 82, was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said.

item.description:

The US removed all its bombers from the UK's RAF Fairford base last month after a major incident in September that police described as "suspicious"ByJack BurgessPublished8 hours ago
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives that it alleges were involved in a string of plots in the US and Europe.
The DOJ said Iranian agents most recently "orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the United Kingdom", saying they were involved in the major incident in September near RAF Fairford in the UK, where US armed forces were stationed.
One man, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, is accused of communicating with contacts in the UK from a prison in New York where he is awaiting trial on previous charges. The other two are accused of doing the same from Iran.
Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the RAF Fairford incident.
Seven men have been arrested in the UK over the incident, which came to light when suspicious vans were reported near the RAF base.
Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and dual Iranian-Iraqi citizen Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi were charged in an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the DOJ said.
It accuses the trio of planning attacks in Europe that were carried out under the name of a purportedly new group with the pseudonym Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (The Islamic Movement of the People of the Right Hand - HAYI).
"Of the 18 terrorist attacks in the spring of 2026 for which HAYI claimed responsibility in Europe, seven took place in the UK," the DOJ statement said. It added that the attacks involved "arsons, explosives, and in one instance, a near-fatal stabbing in London of two Jewish men, including a dual US-British citizen".
Two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London, in April. A suspect is due to stand trial next year.

Spain holds state funeral for 69 killed in high-speed rail crash
Relatives of the 69 people killed in a high-speed rail collision in Spain last month attended a state funeral TuesdayByFRANCISCO SECO Associated Press and SUMAN NAISHADHAM Associated PressNovember 10, 2026, 2:16 PM
TOLEDO, Spain -- Relatives of the 69 people killed in a high-speed rail collision in Spain last month attended a state funeral on Tuesday with Spain's royals, almost two weeks after the crash.
The ceremony took place in the towering 13th-century Toledo Cathedral in central Spain.
The collision happened on Oct. 28 when a high-speed train slammed into another that was stationary on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda, around 140 kilometers (87 miles) south of the capital.
It was the second deadly collision this year involving Spain’s extensive high-speed rail network, shattering Spaniards' trust in the transit system that is regarded as one of the country's crowning achievements.
Under growing pressure, Transport Minister Óscar Puente stepped down last week. His resignation was followed by that of Luis Pedro Marco, who was head of Spain's railway infrastructure operator.
Spain will hold a general election on Nov. 29, in which progressive Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is seeking reelection.
Sánchez did not attend Tuesday's funeral service.
A 16th-century sculpture of Christ was moved from the town of Urda to the cathedral in Toledo for the funeral service.

item.title: [Guardian China] ‘Flying cars’ could launch in China next summer, maker of two-seat model says
item.description:
Aridge unveils new modular 'flying car'
‘Flying cars’ could launch in China next summer, maker of two-seat model says
XPeng says its $300k low-altitude device will soon be ready for emergency services and recreational use in rural areas
People could start taking trips in so-called flying cars in China as soon as next summer, the manufacturer of a two-seater vehicle with autopilot model has said.
Deli Zhao, the chief executive of the Chinese flying car company XPeng, said the $300,000 (£225,000) low-altitude device would be ready for use by recreational users in rural locations and by emergency services in the second half of 2027. After 10 years of development including trials of flying motorbikes at the company’s Guangzhou base, it has been approved by China’s civil aviation authorities for limited use.
The small cockpit is about the size of a Fiat 500 car and the vehicle is lifted into the air by six drone-like battery-powered propellers and steered by a simple joystick. It can also fly autonomously to a programmed destination, but Xhao, a trained pilot, claimed he could teach anyone to fly it in five minutes.
The price tag for the contraption includes a six-wheel van about the size of a Ford Transit, out of the back of which the flying vehicle unfolds “just like the Transformers”, said Zhao. He has been developing flying cars for almost a decade and said he was part-inspired by the flying creatures ridden by humans in the Harry Potter stories and the Green Goblin’s flying skateboard from the Spider-Man comics.
View image in fullscreen
The flying car during a demonstration in Dubai last month. Photograph: Giuseppe Cacace/AFP/Getty Images
“The world where everyone can be a captain is about to arrive,” he said at the Web Summit in Lisbon on Tuesday, where a prototype of the vehicle drew large crowds. Zhao said no one had yet been injured or hurt using the vehicle which, although described as a car, lacks wheels and is better described as a helicopter-style ...

item.title: [Guardian World] Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities
item.description:
Lewis Hamilton with members of the Egyptian Red Crescent near the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and the Gaza Strip Photograph: Reuters
View image in fullscreen
Lewis Hamilton with members of the Egyptian Red Crescent near the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and the Gaza Strip Photograph: Reuters
Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities
Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent
Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.
The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine. I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage,” Hamilton said in October.
A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day.
Israeli forces have continued to advance, expanding their control from 53% of the territory to at least 60%, an independent commission of UN experts said last month.
View image in fullscreen
Lewis Hamilton (in black) listens to an Egyptian Red Crescent official during a visit to a logistics centre in Al-Arish. Photograph: Mohammed Arafat/AP
Airstrikes also continue, and Israeli fire along the advancing front has killed at least 196 Palestinians, including 18 women, 32 boys and 11 girls, the commission said.
Hamilton toured Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with Gaza before visiting logistics warehouses operated by the Egyptian Red Crescent, which facilitates the entry of aid to Gaza.

item.title: [ABC News World] Overnight strikes in Yemen kill at least 1 person and wound 9, and other Mideast news
item.description:
Overnight strikes in Yemen kill at least 1 person and wound 9, and other Mideast news
Overnight strikes in Yemen have hit a gas station and an oil facility, killing at least one person and wounding nine othersByThe Associated PressNovember 10, 2026, 7:06 AM
Overnight strikes hit a gas station and an oil facility in Yemen, killing at least one person and wounding nine, residents and the Iran-backed Houthi rebels said on Tuesday.
In Iran, a top security official claimed that the Iran war had already “wrecked” the United States, and called on Washington to accept seven demands that Tehran has made for an end to the conflict.
Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Tuesday. Read our full coverage here.
Houthi-run health ministry spokesperson Anees al-Asbahi said in a statement on X on Tuesday that a strike hit a gas station in a district of Yemen's capital, Sanaa, killing one person and wounding three others.
He said another airstrike targeted an oil company, wounding at least six people, causing “extensive damage” to nearby homes and shops and panicking residents.
Al-Asbahi blamed Saudi Arabia for both strikes. The Associated Press couldn’t independently verify his claims.
The strikes come amid renewed fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces that escalated this summer. The rebels continue to target Saudi energy facilities and airports as part of a campaign they say is meant to push Saudi Arabia into lifting its blockade on Yemen.
Sanaa resident Khaled al-Khawlani told the AP on Tuesday that he was horrified by the explosions that targeted the oil facility near residential areas of Sanaa at around 4 a.m.
Another resident said the explosions shattered his windows and reverberated across the city while people slept. The resident spoke on condition of anonymity for security reasons.

item.description:
Sheep grazing beneath solar panels at one of the world's largest solar bases, in Hainan Tibetan autonomous prefecture, Qinghai province, China. Photograph: Go Nakamura/Reuters
View image in fullscreen
Sheep grazing beneath solar panels at one of the world's largest solar bases, in Hainan Tibetan autonomous prefecture, Qinghai province, China. Photograph: Go Nakamura/Reuters
US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’
Cop31 live – latest updates
China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.
As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
Green energy is a vital component of the export engine that has kept China’s sluggish post-pandemic economy on track. The success of its exports stands in contrast to its failure to significantly boost domestic general consumption, a structural weakness that has persistently vexed leaders.
In 2025, clean-tech exports surpassed $220bn, and they should grow again this year; the world’s largest emitter is now the world’s leading supplier of clean energy technology. The tech world has spent the day digesting the extraordinary news that Jensen Huang - the charismatic, leather-jacket wearing chief executive of the multi-trillion dollar firm Nvidia - is being investigated by his own company over an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
None of us had that on our bingo cards for 2026.
Huang's alleged romantic affair with Alice Huang (no relation), the former CEO of a Singapore-based data centre company, has cast ripples far beyond his immediate family - undoubtedly on an emotional rollercoaster of their own - taking us to a crossroads at which technology, geopolitics and national security intersect.
In a nutshell, this is about the bitter rivalry between the US and China, as well as whether Jensen Huang has betrayed the US as well as his wife.

item.title: [BBC China] Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description:
Image source, Bloomberg via Getty ImagesByArchie MitchellBusiness reporterPublished9 November 2026
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report, external.
The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week.

item.title: [Guardian World] Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
item.description:
People at the scene of the collision in Giza province. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
People at the scene of the collision in Giza province. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images
Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said.
The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash occurred, said people rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances.
Gamal said he saw about 80 of the injured being taken by ambulances to hospital. Some passengers were trapped inside one of the carriages of the stationary train and died, he said.
View image in fullscreen
People search for survivors after the collision. Photograph: AP
Egypt’s president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, said in a social media post that he had ordered a prompt investigation.

item.title: [Guardian World] How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester
item.description:
Daniel Oyegade on the shoot for Homage, a See My World production. Photograph: Omar Balaa
View image in fullscreen
Daniel Oyegade on the shoot for Homage, a See My World production. Photograph: Omar Balaa
How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives
African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.
See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.
The festival is part of See My World’s year-round programme showcasing pan-African arts, culture and events.
It reflects the determination among creatives and activists in Manchester to build on the legacy of the 1945 Pan-African Congress in Manchester – which connected luminaries of postwar independence movements with a shared vision of liberation – after last year’s 80th anniversary commemorations.
See My World’s CEO and artistic director, Tunde Adekoya, said this month’s film festival was taking inspiration from across the spectrum of pan-African thought, including the works of Kenyan writers John Mbiti, an Anglican theologian who died in 2019, and Ngũgĩ wa Thiong’o, the author of the groundbreaking 1986 book Decolonising the Mind who died last year.
Both writers rejected the colonial conceit that African thought was inferior, stressed the importance of community and saw reclaiming African ways of knowing as essential to a people’s self-understanding.
